import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1113

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1113)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial
  Number Theory. Monographie de l'Enseignement Mathématique, No. 28 (1980).
- [Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe,
  Warsaw (1960).
- [FFK08] Filaseta, M., Finch, C., and Kozek, M., On powers associated with Sierpiński numbers,
  Riesel numbers and Polignac's conjecture. Journal of Number Theory 128 (2008), 1916–1940.

A positive odd integer $k$ is a *Sierpiński number* if $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is composite for all
$n \geq 0$. A *covering set* for $k$ is a finite set of primes $P$ such that every number of
the form $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is divisible by at least one prime in $P$.

Sierpiński (1960) proved that infinitely many Sierpiński numbers exist using covering systems.
The smallest known Sierpiński number is 78557 (Selfridge). Erdős and Graham conjectured that
there exist Sierpiński numbers with no finite covering set. A negative answer would imply
infinitely many Fermat primes.

Note: The notion of a covering set for a Sierpiński number is closely related to a
`CoveringSystem` of $\mathbb{Z}$ (see
`FormalConjecturesForMathlib.NumberTheory.CoveringSystem`): a finite covering set of primes
for $k$ works because the exponents $n$ for which each prime divides $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ form
residue classes whose union covers all of $\mathbb{Z}$, i.e. a covering system.

See also Erdős Problems [203](https://www.erdosproblems.com/203) and
[276](https://www.erdosproblems.com/276).
-/

namespace Erdos1113

/--
A *covering set* for a positive odd integer $k$ is a finite set of primes $P$ such that every
number of the form $k \cdot 2^n + 1$ is divisible by at least one prime in $P$.
-/
def HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : Finset ℕ, (∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime) ∧ ∀ n, ∃ p ∈ P, p ∣ (k * 2 ^ n + 1)

/--
Sierpiński [Si60] proved that there are infinitely many Sierpiński numbers, using covering
systems to construct suitable covering sets for any $k$ satisfying a certain congruence.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/HowieHwong/lean-erdos-proofs/blob/b8b641ba2d00dc4d1fe205a078a4159372672459/Erdos/P1113.lean#L22"]
theorem erdos_1113.variants.infinitely_many_sierpinski :
    Set.Infinite {k : ℕ | k.IsSierpinskiNumber} := by
  sorry

/--
**Erdős Problem 1113.** Do there exist Sierpiński numbers that possess no finite covering set
of primes?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] conjectured that the answer is yes. A negative answer would imply
that there are infinitely many Fermat primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1113 :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧ ¬ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k := by
  sorry

/--
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1113.variants.filaseta_finch_kozek :
    ∀ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber →
      k.IsPerfectPower ∨ HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k := by
  sorry

end Erdos1113

findings.description: The bibliography at lines 26–27 identifies [Si60] as Sierpiński's Elementary Theory of Numbers, Warsaw (1960). The cited 1960 infinitude result actually comes from his journal article “Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n + 1.” This is a reference error only; the mathematical statement, attribution, and year of the infinitude theorem are correct.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Si60 identifies the article in Elemente der Mathematik (1960), pp. 73–74. The original article, Elemente der Mathematik 15 (1960), pp. 73–74, DOI 10.5169/seals-20713, states and proves the infinitude theorem. Filaseta–Finch–Kozek also cite this article as reference [12].
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the [Si60] entry with: Sierpiński, W., Sur un problème concernant les nombres k·2^n + 1. Elemente der Mathematik 15 (1960), 73–74. Optionally include https://doi.org/10.5169/seals-20713.

reformulations.difference: ErGr80, p. 27, asks whether every such sequence has a positive integer N sharing a nontrivial factor with every positive-exponent term. Lean asks for a Sierpiński number without a finite prime covering set, and includes exponent zero. This matches the positive existence question on the current Erdős Problems page.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite prime cover gives the common-factor integer N by multiplying its primes. Conversely, the prime divisors of a positive common-factor integer form a finite prime cover. A cover for positive exponents extends to exponent zero by adjoining a prime divisor of k+1. The Sierpiński definitions with positive and nonnegative exponents also agree: k=1 fails at exponent one, and for odd k>1 the additional term k+1 is composite. Thus existence without a finite cover is precisely a counterexample to the book's universal common-factor assertion. Proved as Review1113.main_rhs_iff_original in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: Conjecture 3 of the author manuscript says that a Sierpiński number which is not a power ℓ^r, with ℓ≥1 and r>1, has its least prime divisor of k·2^n+1 bounded as n tends to infinity. Lean instead states the disjunction of being a perfect power and possessing a finite prime cover.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite cover bounds the least prime divisor by its largest prime. Conversely, an eventual bound gives a finite list of possible least prime divisors for the tail; adjoining the finitely many least prime divisors from the initial terms gives a finite cover. All terms exceed one, so these are genuine prime divisors. Sierpiński numbers exceed one, making the source's allowance ℓ=1 immaterial. Positive versus nonnegative exponents is harmless as explained above, and the disjunction is classically equivalent to the conditional statement for non-perfect-powers. The full equivalence was proved as Review1113.ffk_conjecture_iff in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked; no mathematical misformalization was found. The recorded statuses agree with the sources. Boundary tests exclude k=0,1,2,3 as Sierpiński numbers and rule out an empty prime cover. Small perfect-power and composite cases were evaluated, and the concrete Sierpiński number 78557 and its prime cover were verified in Lean. The cited external infinitude proof was compiled against the local Mathlib after moving its import before the module docstring; its statement and proof body were unchanged, and its axioms were only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The equivalence proofs also use only those standard axioms. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, equivalences.lean, and external_proof_check.lean. No repository files were edited.
